issues.legal_issue: A dependent relation who ordinarily resides with a member of the armed services cannot use the special eviction procedure on the basis of that relationship when the member has retired and remains alive.
material_facts: The applicants were adult daughters of a retired service member and claimed that they were dependent on him and ordinarily resided with him.
After their father had retired, the applicants sought recovery of rented premises for occupation through the special eviction procedure.
Their father was alive when they brought the eviction proceedings.
issues.conclusion: The applicants could not maintain their eviction application under the special procedure. The appeal was dismissed, without preventing them from pursuing any other remedy available by law.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 13(1)(ff) and 29B of the West Bengal Premises Tenancy Act, 1956, as amended in 1979, a dependent relation who ordinarily resides with a service member falls within the relevant category for the special procedure only where the member dies while in service or within five years of retirement. The wording and structure of Section 29B, including the contrast between “a member” and “such member” and the corresponding provisos, support that construction. The Court relied on Central Bank of India v. Ravindra, (2002) 1 SCC 367, for the interpretive significance of “such” as referring to something previously mentioned. Where statutory language is plain and explicit, an assumed legislative intent cannot be used to enlarge it to include a category the legislature did not provide for.

predicates.special_eviction_application: The landlord sought recovery of rented premises through a special eviction process.
predicates.dependent_co_resident_relation: The applicant was a dependent relation who ordinarily resided with a member of the armed services.
predicates.member_retired_alive: The service member had retired and remained alive when the applicant sought recovery.

issues.definition: When a dependent relation who ordinarily lived with a service member seeks recovery through a special eviction process after that member has retired and remains alive, the special process is unavailable.
